reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4) depicts Yahweh responding with compassion to the people's suffering in Egypt. God declares 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people...and have heard their cry' and commits 'I have come down to deliver them.' The only divine anger expressed in the text is directed at Moses for his hesitation and excuses ('the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses'), not at the people themselves. Throughout, Yahweh provides signs and miracles to authenticate Moses' mission to lead the people to freedom, demonstrating commitment to their deliverance rather than complaint about their conduct.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
